counting: Requirements that no available fixture can exercise on the frozen x86-64 builds. Each reason is the requirement gap in tests/parity-vm/deferrals.json.

limits.reason: Not applicable in a VM; the PTY is the terminal under test. Physical serial/console hardware would need real hardware and is out of scope for a disposable VM.

The kernel truncates records written to /dev/kmsg to about 1 KiB, so no record near the 8192-byte read size can exist on the live ring; that boundary is exercised only through the fixture-file path (legacy/dmesg/split-read-boundary)

The 74 GraphemeBreakTest lines containing U+0000 cannot be passed to the utf8 builtin: its TEXT operand is a bash word, and a bash word is a NUL-terminated C string, so a NUL code point cannot be represented in any argument.

The password half of PermitRootLogin prohibit-password versus yes is decided by the /dev/bashos-auth kernel authority (BSSHD_AUTH_DEV in sshd.c), which the disposable guest does not provide; without it no password attempt can be told apart from a refusal, and a stand-in authority would not test the real one. Admitted root command execution is covered by the privilege=root case.

Debian 13's cloud and generic amd64 kernels (6.12.113+deb13), the only kernels the guest images can boot, are both built without CONFIG_UCLAMP_TASK, so /proc/sys/kernel/sched_util_clamp_min and sched_util_clamp_max do not exist
bashpoll is compiled into both candidate builds; enable -d fails with "not dynamically loaded", so the unload hook cannot be reached.
Non-SSE2 x86 target: SSE2 is part of the x86-64 baseline and only x86-64 binaries are shipped, so no non-SSE2 build or CPU target exists.

Not reachable through the candidate interface: the fixed wgetch.c bw_keys table (no fixture or terminfo loading) contains no exact key that is also a prefix of a longer key (e.g. ESC[20~ and ESC[200~ diverge at byte 5), so the exact-vs-longer resolution path in bw_read_key_fd cannot be triggered by any input. Requires a candidate key-table extension, not a fixture.
